title: Other Sheep
summary: Jesus tells the gathered people of other sheep who have not heard his voice or seen him, and says he will go to them so they may become one fold with one shepherd.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus says that he has other sheep not of this land or Jerusalem and that he has not manifested himself to them.
The Father commanded Jesus to go to them; they will hear his voice and be numbered among his sheep, forming one fold with one shepherd.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus is visibly speaking to the people present at Bountiful.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and setting of the other sheep are not described; do not depict them as a present scene.

spoken_dialogue.text: I have other sheep which are not of this land
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The other sheep are described in speech, not shown as a separate event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Jesus visiting the other sheep in this scene.

title: Write These Sayings
summary: Jesus commands the people to write his sayings after he is gone, describing how the record will reach the Gentiles and the scattered remnant and how he will gather Israel.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus commands the people to write his sayings after he is gone.
The sayings will be kept and manifested to the Gentiles; the remnant may come to a knowledge of Jesus, their Redeemer.
Jesus says he will gather them from the four quarters of the earth and fulfill the Father's covenant with Israel.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus is visibly delivering the command to write.
unspecified_visual_details: No writing action or written record is explicitly described as occurring now.

spoken_dialogue.text: I command you that ye shall write these sayings after I am gone
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Future dissemination and gathering are teachings, not events shown as happening in this moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict future readers, a written record being produced, or a gathering scene.

title: Blessed Are the Believing Gentiles
summary: Jesus teaches that believing Gentiles are blessed and that, because of their belief and Israel's unbelief, truth will later come to the Gentiles.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus says believing Gentiles are blessed because of their belief and the Holy Ghost's witness of him and the Father.
The Father says truth will come to the Gentiles in the latter day because of their belief and Israel's unbelief.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus is visibly teaching the people present.
unspecified_visual_details: No Gentiles or latter-day events are described as physically present.

spoken_dialogue.text: And blessed are the Gentiles, because of their belief in me
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The latter-day coming of truth is a prediction, not a present-tense scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Holy Ghost in a visible form; no appearance is stated.

title: Warning to the Gentiles
summary: Jesus relays the Father's warning that the Gentiles will scatter and oppress Israel, while Israel will be smitten, afflicted, slain, cast out, and despised.

explicit_facts.text: The Gentiles scatter Israel and Israel is cast out and trodden underfoot by them.
Israel is described as smitten, afflicted, slain, cast out, hated, and made a hiss and a byword.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus is visibly speaking to the people present.
unspecified_visual_details: The narrated future oppression is not shown as a present event; no setting or individual victims are specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: my people who are of the house of Israel have been cast out from among them
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses report and predict suffering; they do not place those events in the current scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage violence or invent specific Gentile or Israelite individuals.

title: The Gospel Withdrawn
summary: Jesus declares that if the Gentiles reject the fulness of his gospel and persist in wickedness, the gospel will be brought from among them and brought to Israel.

explicit_facts.text: The Father says the gospel will be brought from among the Gentiles if they sin against it, reject its fulness, and persist in the listed evils.
The Father will remember his covenant with Israel and bring his gospel to them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus is visibly delivering the warning.
unspecified_visual_details: The future rejection and transfer of the gospel are not depicted as occurring in the moment.

spoken_dialogue.text: I will bring the fulness of my gospel from among them
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The list of sins is part of a conditional warning.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict specific acts of sin or a future transfer scene.

title: Israel and the Repentant Gentiles
summary: Jesus states that Israel will know the fulness of the gospel and that repentant Gentiles may be numbered among Israel; he contrasts this with the fate of those who will not turn and hearken.

explicit_facts.text: The Gentiles will not have power over Israel, and Israel will come to know the fulness of the gospel.
Repentant Gentiles will be numbered among Israel.
The Father says he will not suffer Israel to tread down the Gentiles in one case; if they will not turn and hearken, Israel will go through among them and tread them down.
Those refusing to turn are compared to salt that has lost its savor.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus is visibly teaching the people present.
unspecified_visual_details: The conditional future outcomes and the salt comparison are not shown literally.

spoken_dialogue.text: if the Gentiles will repent and return unto me
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The salt imagery is a figure of speech, not a literal scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal salt being trodden or future conflict.

title: The Land for an Inheritance
summary: Jesus says the Father commanded him to give this people the land for their inheritance, then introduces the words of Isaiah.

explicit_facts.text: The Father commanded Jesus to give this people this land for their inheritance.
Jesus introduces the words of the prophet Isaiah.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus is visibly speaking to the people present.
unspecified_visual_details: The land's borders and appearance are not specified here.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Isaiah's words are quoted in the following scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent borders, landmarks, or a land-distribution event.

title: Zion and Jerusalem Redeemed
summary: Jesus quotes Isaiah: watchmen sing when the Lord brings Zion again; Jerusalem's waste places rejoice because the Lord comforts and redeems his people; all nations see God's salvation.

explicit_facts.text: Isaiah's words describe watchmen lifting their voices and singing when the Lord brings Zion again.
Isaiah's words call Jerusalem's waste places to joy because the Lord has comforted his people and redeemed Jerusalem.
Isaiah's words say the Lord's holy arm is made bare before the nations and all the earth will see God's salvation.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus is visibly quoting Isaiah to the people present.
unspecified_visual_details: Watchmen, Jerusalem's waste places, and the Lord's arm are not described as present visual events.

spoken_dialogue.text: Thy watchmen shall lift up the voice
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophetic quotations, not a narrated scene of their fulfillment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord's arm as a literal visible limb or stage future fulfillment as happening now.
